text.2_Daf, 0_Line, 3_Comment: And if you will say, "but we learned that the spouse of a priest or a girl (who got married at an age) less than 3 have only one doubt!", like we will say in the Gemara later on, "but other women have a doubt on the doubt! So why should they get married on Wednesday? And the Rabenu Tam responds: The rabbis do not differentiate (the cases of) the decree. And because of the spouse of a priest and the girl (who got married at an age) less than 3, we decree for all women to get married on Wednesday. ---Incomplete---
text.32_Daf, 0_Line, 0_Comment: The bride as she is: And if she has a blemish, they are quiet and they do not praise it. And also (another possibility is) they praise her with something pleasant that she has - for example, [he praises her] about her eyes or her hands if they are beautiful. And Beit Hillel says that you praise her altogether, as when we mention that which she has to be praised, it implies that the rest is to be denigrated.
text.164_Daf, 0_Line, 0_Comment: In Bava Batra we have a Mishna that states that "A Husband may not establish a Hazakah on the property of his wife". The Gemorra proceeds to question this statement of the Mishna and say it is Obvious/Pshita. Since the Rabannan allowed the husband to reap that benefit, (the Rabannan cannot also allow him to establish a Hazakah through that benefit. Rule: Anyone that derives benefit from a property for 3 years and is uncontested, establishes a Hazakah and may now acquire that property). The Gemorra then proceeds to answer the Kasha and say that this is a case where the husband wrote to his wife "Din uDvarim Ein Li BeNekhasaikh". And now someone would have mistakenly thought that since the husband can no longer reap the benefit from his wife's property he may be able to establish the Hazakah (in an unspecified way) over his wife's property. So Hiddush of the Mishna is to say No he cannot. The problem is that in our Mishna in Ketubot saying this statement "Din uDvarim Ein Li BeNekhasaikh" does not stop the husband's ability to derive benefit from his wife's estate. The language needed is "Din uDvarim Ein Li BeNekhasaikh uBePeirotehen". Tosfot answers and says "Lav Davka" This is what the Gemorra in Bava Batra meant.
text.184_Daf, 15_Line, 0_Comment: "I do not agree with Rabbi Natan, rather, they divide the estate equally." Rabbeinu Hananel ruled according to Rabbi Yehuda Hanasi understood the division as follows:  it is unimaginable that when there are only 300 dinar available, that the one claiming a hundred receives 100, the one claiming two hundred receives 100, and the one claiming three hundred receives 100. The principle of justice is lacking here! Rather, what Rabbi Yehuda Hanasi must mean is that each of the dinars that they are owed have equal power. Therefore, the estate of the deceased is divided into six. The one owed one hundred takes one part, the one owed two hundred takes two parts, and the one owed three hundred takes three parts. Each of them claims according to the money owed to her until they come as close as possible to being payed. This is justice, and this is what he must have meant.
text.219_Daf, 13_Line, 0_Comment: He says to go up [to the Land of Israel], etc.: It is not practiced in our times, as there is danger on the roads. And Rabbenu Chaim says that today, it is not a commandment to live in the Land of Israel, as there are several commandments that are dependent upon the land - and several punishments - that we are not able to be careful about and to be cognizant of.
